DI BACONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.gov.ph OPINION NO. HON. RUEL G. MOLINA, JD Municipal Mayor Municipality of Kumalarang Zamboanga del Sur Dear Mayor Molina: This has reference to your letter dated February 20, 2024, concerning Sangguniang Panlalawigan Resolution No. 1512-2024, which invalidated Municipal Ordinance No. 14 Series of 2023 of Kumalarang, Zamboanga del Sur, "An Ordinance Revising the Municipal Order No. 7 Series of 2023 Entitled "Authorizing the Loan of the Municipality of Kumalarang, Zamboanga del Sur, in the Total Amount of Two Hundred Fifty-Two Million (Php 252,000,000.00) with the Development Bank of the Philippines for the Purpose/s State Therein." Culled from your letter are the pertinent factual antecedents: The Provincial Government of Zamboanga del Sur, under the leadership of Governor Victor J. Yu, has lent the Municipality of Kumalarang equipment necessary for the creation of roadways. However, Governor Yu pulled out all the pieces of equipment when your relationship was strained. Consequently, the project of creating roadways in far- flung areas was left incomplete. The Municipality of Kumalarang was constrained to endeavour other legal means to ensure the continuity of the roadway project, including securing a loan agreement through Municipal Ordinance No. 7, Series of 2023, entitled "An Ordinance Authorizing the Loan of the Municipality of Kumalarang, Zamboanga del Sur, in the Total Amount of Two Hundred Fifty-Two Million (Php 252,000,000.00) with the Development Bank of the Philippines for the Purpose/s State Therein." However, the herein concerned Sanguniang Panlalawigan (SP), in its Resolution No. 1512-2024 dated January 18, 2024, invalidated the said Municipal Ordinance on the following grounds: (1) non-compliance with the Internal Rules; and (2) non-support of the Ordinance by the four (4) Sangguniang Bayan (SB) Members of the Municipality of Kumalarang, Zamboanga del Sur. In response to the said SP Resolution, the Municipality of Kumalarang submitted a letter to the SP to reconsider its invalidation of the subject Municipal Ordinance. Ostensibly, the said request for reconsideration was not acted upon. Hence, on October 9, 2023, the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) members enacted and approved "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54



Municipal Ordinance No. 14 Series of 2023—An Ordinance Revising the Municipal Oder No. 7 Series of 2023. On October 17, 2023, a Letter of Transmittal was submitted to the SP, attaching Municipal Ordinance No. 14, Series of 2023, for perusal and approval by the However, the SP Committee on Rules, Laws, and Privileges, in its Committee Report No. 843-2024 dated January 17, 2024, also invalidated Municipal Ordinance No. 14, Series of 2023, on the grounds that said Ordinance did not meet the majority as required by the Local Government Code and thus could not be made a basis for contracting a loan. Hence, the following issues are proffered for this Department's opinion: I. Whether or not Municipal Ordinance No. 14 Series of 2023 is presumed consistent with the law and therefore valid because it was not acted within the reglementary period of 30 days; and 2. Whether or not the IPMR, though naturally vacant because of the death of the IPMR Representative, is counted in determining the "qualified majority". On the first issue, as represented, the Municipal Ordinance was enacted and approved by the SB on October 9, 2023. Thereafter, it was submitted to the SP on October 17, 2023. However, it was only on January 18, 2024, that the SP issued its Resolution No. 1512-2024, invalidating the subject Municipal Ordinance. Section 56 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (hereafter referred to as the Code) provides for the manner, procedure, timeline, and extent of the SP power vis-å-vis the review of ordinances enacted by the component cities and municipalities, thus: "Section 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sanggunian panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after the receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period of ten (IO) days from receipt of the documents, inform the sangguniang panlalawigan in writing of his comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the sangguniang panlalawigan in making its decision. (c) If the sangguniang panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The sangguniang panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. (d) If no action has been taken by the sangguniang panlalawigan within thirty Page 2 Of 4

(30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid." The aforecited provision is no less instructive. The law stipulates a reglementary period of thirty (30) days within which SP must take action on ordinances submitted to it by SB. In our previous opinions, we have belabored that compliance with such a reglementary period is mandatory so much so that anything short thereof eventuates to the validity of the legislative measures reviewed—this is the clear import of the aforequoted provision. Accordingly, within thirty (30) days after submission of the municipal ordinance and after receipt thereof by the SP, the SP must act thereon. This Department has time and time again opined that the action to be taken consists of declaring the ordinance invalid in whole or in part for being ultra vires. If no action is taken by the SP within the reglementary period, the ordinance being reviewed is then presumed valid and consistent with the law. In the present case, the days are reckoned from October 17, 2023, to January 18, 2024, which is beyond the 30-day period required by law. Such being the case, the subject Municipal Ordinance should now be deemed consistent with the law and valid. As to the second issue, we answer in the negative. While Article 107(g) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Code explicitly provides, and as ruled by the Supreme Court in Municipality of Corella Philkonstrakl, that a qualified majority—wherein the total membership of the sanggunian duly elected and qualified regardless of whether all of them were present or not in a particular session is considered in determining a majority—is required in the passage of an ordinance authorizing or directing the payment of money, such as the subject Municipal Ordinance in question, the same should not be construed to include the vote of a deceased sanggunian member in determining a majority; to do otherwise would be legally and logically absurd as it would be tantamount to attributing voting rights to a non-existent being. It may be well to note that positions, such as the Indigenous Peoples Mandatory Representative (IPMR), are not abstract—positions or offices are operated by individuals who perform essential functions appurtenant thereto. Stated differently, when an official or individual holding a position dies, the position itself is deemed non- existent. A vacant position or office is bereft of capacity to function or carry out its duties and responsibilities without an individual assuming such positions. This is precisely, to our mind, the legislative intent of the inclusion of a particular chapter in the Code, which specifically deals with matters regarding vacancies and successions to ensure stability in the operation of local governments. In the present case, it is established that the IPMR of the herein concerned municipality has passed away. Accordingly, his death created a permanent vacancy in the SB. Such being the case, until the new IPMR has duly assumed office, the IPMR should not be counted in the determination of the qualified majority. It is to be emphasized, however, that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government, and as such, it is devoid of authority to declare invalid or illegal any legislative measures enacted or passed by local government 1 G.R No. 218663, dated February 28, 2022 Page 3 of 4

officials, nor does it have the authority to declare invalid or illegal any acts committed by local government officials that are alleged to be in violation of the Local Government Code or any other applicable laws. The same must be threshed out in the proper forum. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, y the A hority of the Secr tary: AT N VICTOR R.
